children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--ICE Futures canola contracts were sharply higher at midday Tuesday.
November canola was up C$12.10 at C$834.60 per tonne, trading well above its major moving averages.

Gains in crude oil amid the heightened conflict in the Middle East underpinned world vegetable oil markets, with strength in Chicago soyoil and European rapeseed futures contributing to the firmer tone in canola.
The Canadian oilseed outpaced the other markets to the upside.
Heavy rains across the Prairies over the weekend added to the strength in canola, as the untimely moisture flooded some fields and raised concerns over potential harvest delays.
Statistics Canada will release ending stocks estimates for the 2025-26 marketing year on Wednesday. The agency's first production estimates for 2026-27 will be out the following week.
An estimated 33,700 canola contracts traded as of 11:36 EDT.
